had surgery on my foot on 12.11. After a week of being unwell, I rang my GP surgery to book a telephone appointment or home visit with the doctor to request another sick note. Despite explaining to the receptionist that I could not walk or drive, she told me I had to come into the surgery, which I eventually did because I had no other choice.
After another week, I went back to the surgery to have my stitches removed, and unfortunately my wound opened during the removal. The nurse applied a dressing and advised me to rest.
When my sick note ran out on 30.11, I contacted the surgery again to request an extension, as I am still unable to return to work. I went to the surgery twice on Monday and then called again on Tuesday morning, only to be told that the request was still with the doctor. It is now Wednesday I still have not heard anything about my sick note.
I eventually had to go back to the hospital, where I was told that my wound was still in a bad condition. I cannot stand or walk, and I need to be off work for at least another two weeks. Luckily, the doctor at the hospital issued a sick note for me, because my GP surgery—especially the reception staff—has been completely unhelpful. I understand that they may not have had the hospital records yet, but they should still believe the patient, especially since a GP had already previously issued me a sick note. Writing another one is a simple task that takes only a few minutes.
I am still waiting for any information from the surgery. There is more than one doctor working there, yet nothing has been done. When I asked the receptionist to check whether my request was on my record, she said yes, although I doubt she actually looked it up. They often cannot spell my name, and she did not ask for my address or date of birth to confirm my identity. They do not seem to care that without this sick note, I would not be paid by my employer.
The receptionists have no medical experience and are often rude. I rarely need to use this surgery, but when I do, the reception staff are never helpful.
